title: Matheson Wells: Depth and Drilling Cost
meta_description: Matheson well records show a 190-foot median depth, 10 gpm median yield, and finished well costs of $15,500-$25,300.
h1: Matheson, Colorado Well Depths, Yields, and Costs
intro_html:
Buying land around Matheson means dealing with a mix of Denver Basin sedimentary bedrock, fractured-bedrock wells, Laramie Fox Hills wells, and alluvial wells. Within 5 miles of Matheson, Colorado DWR records list 306 permitted wells, with 178 recorded as constructed.

The available records point to a median well depth of 190 feet and a median reported yield of 10.0 gallons per minute. Those figures are useful for planning, but they are not a guarantee for a particular lot. Nearby wells, the intended use, site access, and the exact aquifer can change the drilling plan and final cost.

sections.heading: Matheson well depths depend on the aquifer and lot
sections.html:
The median reported well depth near Matheson is 190 feet. The middle half of wells falls from 60 to 285 feet, so a driller bidding a new well should not treat 190 feet as a fixed target. The records also include wells reaching 443 feet at the 90th percentile and a deepest recorded well of 700 feet.

Depths are spread across the area: 35% are under 100 feet, 44% are between 100 and 300 feet, 20% are between 300 and 600 feet, and 1% are deeper than 600 feet. All recorded wells are in the Denver Basin aquifer system. The named formations include fractured bedrock, Laramie Fox Hills, and alluvial wells, which helps explain why neighboring properties can require different drilling depths.

sections.heading: What Matheson wells produce for household use
sections.html:
Among the 112 Matheson-area well records reporting pump yield, the median is 10.0 gallons per minute. The middle half runs from 5.0 to 13.0 gallons per minute. That is a workable planning range for many domestic systems, but the tested production of the specific well matters more than the area median.

Yield records show 58% producing 5 to 15 gallons per minute, 18% producing more than 15 gallons per minute, and 24% producing 1 to 5 gallons per minute. No reported wells are under 1 gallon per minute. A buyer should still ask for the well construction report, pump information, and any pumping or recovery test before assuming the supply will support a home, livestock, irrigation, or future additions. Permitted use controls what the well may legally serve.

sections.heading: The Matheson water table has limited recorded history
sections.html:
Only 18 wells report a static water level, so the local water-level data set is small. The reported median depth to water is 60 feet, with the middle half from 39 to 218 feet. That wide range is a reason to check the records for the adjoining parcels rather than using one water-level figure for the whole Matheson area.

The permit totals by decade do not establish a falling or rising water table. They show permits issued from the 1950s through the 2020s, with the newest permit year listed as 2025, but permit activity is not the same as a water-level trend. For a purchase, compare static water levels, well age, pumping history, and construction reports for nearby wells. A Colorado DWR file review can also identify the permitted use and any conditions attached to the well.

sections.heading: Who has drilled around Matheson and how old are the records
sections.html:
Hamacher Well Works Inc, listed with Alan Ray Hamacher, is the most active driller in these records, with 108 wells. O.K. Hamacher Well Works, listed with Omar K. Hamacher, appears on 17 records, and Eastwood Drilling, listed with Francis Eastwood, appears on 10.

The area has a long permit history: 3 permits in the 1950s, 9 in the 1960s, 26 in the 1970s, 28 in the 1980s, 32 in the 1990s, 63 in the 2000s, 32 in the 2010s, and 18 in the 2020s. Older permits may have less complete construction, yield, or water-level information. The driller named on a historic report is useful local context, but a current bid should be based on the proposed site and present access conditions.

sections.heading: Matheson drilling cost starts with the planned depth
sections.html:
The cost model for Matheson ground uses a typical drilling rate of $50-$70 per foot. At the 190-foot median depth, the drilled hole works out to about $9,500-$13,300. That is the hole only, not the complete water system.

A finished well with pump, pressure tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $15,500-$25,300 at the median depth. A deeper-than-typical hole can move the bid higher, and difficult access or site-specific construction requirements can affect the total. When comparing estimates, confirm the assumed depth, casing and grout scope, pump size, storage equipment, trench length, electrical work, testing, and permit services. The 60-to-285-foot middle-half range shows why a single flat price is not reliable for every Matheson parcel.

sections.heading: Checks that matter before building near Matheson
sections.html:
Low yield is not the main pattern in the reported records, but a buyer should not rely on the area median. Dry holes, lower-than-expected production, poor recovery, and unsuitable water quality remain site-specific risks. Fractured-bedrock conditions can be especially unpredictable, while Laramie Fox Hills and alluvial records may reflect different drilling conditions.

Environmental screening also deserves attention. Mapped sites within about 10 miles include 2 PFAS sampling or contamination sites and 3 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. There are 0 historic mine features in that mapped search. Test the water from the actual well for the intended household use, and review septic setbacks, drainfield space, access for drilling equipment, and the proposed building location. A permitted household-use well does not remove the need to confirm the permit terms or water quality.

faq.q: How deep are wells in Matheson, Colorado?
faq.a: The median reported well depth within 5 miles of Matheson is 190 feet. The middle half runs from 60 to 285 feet, while the 90th-percentile depth is 443 feet and the deepest recorded well is 700 feet. Depth varies with the lot and the Denver Basin formation reached, so neighboring well reports are important before budgeting.

faq.q: How much does it cost to drill a well in Matheson?
faq.a: The local drilling model uses $50-$70 per foot. At the 190-foot median depth, the drilled hole is estimated at $9,500-$13,300. A finished well with pump, tank, trenching, and electrical is estimated at $15,500-$25,300. Ask each driller what depth and included equipment the estimate assumes.

faq.q: How much water do wells produce in Matheson?
faq.a: The median reported pump yield is 10.0 gallons per minute, based on 112 records. The middle half is 5.0-13.0 gallons per minute. Records show 24% producing 1-5 gallons per minute, 58% producing 5-15, and 18% above 15. These are area records, not a guarantee for a new well.

faq.q: Is well water safe in Matheson, Colorado?
faq.a: Safety cannot be determined from well depth or yield alone. Mapped environmental sites within about 10 miles include 2 PFAS sampling or contamination sites and 3 EPA Superfund or cleanup sites. Have the actual well tested before drinking it, review nearby land uses, and check the well construction and permit records with Colorado DWR.

faq.q: Do Matheson wells have enough water for a new home?
faq.a: Many reported wells produce in the 5.0-13.0 gallon-per-minute middle range, but the specific well and its permit control the answer. Confirm the permitted use, construction report, pump yield, and recovery information. If planning livestock, irrigation, or additional buildings, verify that the permit allows those uses; household-use wells are not automatically available for every purpose.
